result:
I’d remove the shame from being wrong.

Not the responsibility—people should still repair the harm they cause—but the humiliation that makes admitting error feel like losing yourself. So much damage comes from people defending positions they privately doubt because changing course would mean ridicule, exile, or defeat.

If people could say “I was wrong” and keep their dignity, they might learn faster, forgive more readily, and build institutions capable of correcting themselves.

It wouldn’t end disagreement. It would just stop every disagreement from becoming a battle over who deserves respect.
